Cattle Rally into the Weekend, as Cash Firms

October 16, 2026

Live cattle futures caught some strength on Friday, with contracts up $1.10 to $1.65 at the close. December was up $1.30 on the week. USDA reported northern dressed sales at $350-355 and $222-227 live. Southern sales were reported at $228. The Friday morning Fed Cattle Exchange online auction showed sales of $228-228.50 on 571 of the 2,596 head offered, with a few $224-228.50 bids. Feeder cattle futures ended Friday with mixed action, as most contracts were 25 cents to $1.70 higher and November down a nickel, both on Friday and the week. The CME Feeder Cattle Index was another 90 cents higher on October 15 to $343.54. 

Friday’s Commitment of Traders report from CFTC showed managed money trimming 2,172 contracts from their net long in live cattle futures and options in the week of 10/13, taking it to 47,748 contracts. In feeder cattle futures and options, specs added a modest 65 contracts to their net long as of Tuesday at 8,852 contracts.

USDA Export Sales data showed 19,766 MT of beef sold in the week ending on 10/8 for 2026. Shipments were 12,872 MT in that week a 14-week high.

Wholesale Boxed Beef prices were mixed in the Friday afternoon report, with the Chc/Sel at $19.26. Choice boxes were down $1.67 to $372.31, with Select 43 cents higher to $353.05. USDA estimated Federally inspected cattle slaughter for this week at 553,000 head through Saturday. That is now up just 2,000 from the week prior but 26,191 head below the same week last year.

Wheat Weakness Extends into the Weekend

October 16, 2026

The wheat complex headed into the weekend holding onto the weakness on Friday. Chicago SRW contracts fell lower on Friday, with contracts down 1 ½ to 9 ½ cents on the day and December losing 10 ½ cents this week. KC HRW futures slipped back 3 to 9 cents at the close, as the lead December contracts was down 15 ¼ cents from last Friday. MPLS spring wheat was down 5 ¼ to 9 ¾ cents on Friday, with December losing 18 ¾ cents on the week.

USDA’s Export Sales report from this morning showed 319,901 MT of wheat sold in the week of October 8. That was down 29.16% from a week ago and 47.89% below the same week last year. The top buyer was Taiwan at 105,800 MT, with 68,100 MT sold to Sri Lanka and 52,300 MT to Mexico.

Weekly CFTC data indicated 3,495 contracts added to the managed money net short in Chicago wheat futures and options as of Tuesday, taking it to 33,038 contracts. In KC wheat, spec traders cut back another 6,649 contracts from their net long to 17,391 contracts.

The FranceAgriMer estimates the country’s wheat crop at 15% planted by October 12.

Weekly CTC data showed managed money adding 1,862 contracts to their net long position in cotton futures and option as of 10/13, taking it to 65,699 contracts.

USDA’s Export Sales report showed 146,892 RB of cotton sales in the week ending in October 8, which was down 11.12% from last week. Costa Rica was the buyer of 74,300 RB, with 21,300 RB to India and 19,800 RB to Pakistan. Sales for 2027/28 were 7,182 RB. Shipments were tallied at 140,561 RB, which was back down 13.11% from last week and a 0.94% increase from the same week last year. Vietnam was the top destination of 40,800 RB, with 20,100 RB to India.

The Seam reported 404 bales sold on October 15, at an average of 73.56 cents/lb. The Cotlook A index was raised by 20 points on Thursday at 91.45. Soybeans Slip Lower into the Weekend as Export Buying Continues

October 16, 2026

Soybeans pulled off early losses on Friday, as contracts were down 1 ¾ to 3 cents in the front month and up ½ to 1 ¾ cents in the deferreds. November was 30 ¾ cents lower for the week. We are over halfway through October, as the average close for November has been $12.83, with the harvest price option for price insurance getting discovered. The cmdtyView national average Cash Bean price was down 1 ¼ cents at $12.03 1/2. Soymeal futures were down $1 to $3.10, with Dec slipping $8.50 this week. Soy Oil futures were anywhere from down 2 to 25 points higher, as December was 89 points lower for the week.

USDA confirmed another round of private export sales of 558,000 MT of soybeans to China this morning, taking this week’s total to 1.358 MMT to China. There was another 236,000 MT to unknown destinations, with the total to unknown sales announced this week at 519,450 MT.

Export Sales data indicated 574,878 MT of wheat sales in the week ending on October 8. That was up just 4.64% from last week but 26.77% below the same week last year. China was the buyer pf 126,300 MT, with 110,700 MT sold to Egypt and 110,000 MT to Bangladesh.

Soybean meal sales were tallied at 366,314 MT, which was on the middle of the estimated range of 200,000 to 600,000 MT. Bean oil sales came in at 1,208 MT, compared to trade estimates of 0-10,000 MT.

CFTC data from Friday showed spec funds trimming 14,169 contracts from their net long position in soybean futures and options as of Tuesday. That took their net long to 237,491 contracts by October 13.

Weakness in the Corn Market Continues on Friday Trade

October 16, 2026

Corn prices are down 1 to 2 cents as futures round out the week of trade. Futures faced late pressure on Thursday, with contracts closing down 1 to 4 cents at the closing bell. Open interest was down 5,434 contracts on Thursday, heavily in the December contract. The CmdtyView national average Cash Corn price was down 2 1/2 cents at $4.38 1/2. 

EIA data from Thursday showed ethanol production in the week of October 9 at 1.065 million barrels per day, up 12,000 bpd on the week. Ethanol stocks were up 199,000 barrels to 23.942 million barrels. Refiner inputs were up 2,000 bpd to 899,000 bpd, as exports of ethanol slipped back by 45,000 bpd to 121,000 bpd.

USDA’s Export Sales report will be out this morning, as traders are looking for a range of 0.5-1.2 MMT for 2026/27 corn sales in the week of 10/8 per a Reuters survey. Bookings for 2027/28 are seen in a range of 0-50,000 MT. 

CONAB data from this morning showed the 2026/27 corn crop at 148 MMT, up 2.4% from a year ago if realized. USDA is at 139 MMT. The first crop is taking up a larger part of the increase, up 8.9% to 32.1 MMT. Much of that was via a 10.72% jump in acreage.

A South Korean importer purchased 134,000 MT of optional origin corn in a private deal overnight. China set their official import tariff rate quota at 7.2 MMT for 2027, consistent with their previous TRQ.

Losses in Soybeans Extending to Friday Morning

October 16, 2026

Soybeans are showing extended weakness on Friday morning, with losses of 4 to 6 cents. Futures fell further into the close on Thursday, down 10 to 14 ¼ cents as futures faded Chinese purchases and sell a bearish NOPA report. Open interest was up 3,241 contracts on Thursday, with November down 6,366 contracts. The cmdtyView national average Cash Bean price was down 14 1/2 cents at $12.04. Soymeal futures were down $1.20 to $4.70, with Soy Oil futures up 9 points to 21 points lower. 

USDA confirmed private export sales of 330,000 MT of soybeans to China on Thursday, all for 2026/27, with 283,450 MT sold to unknown destinations during the reporting period. That took the total announced for the week to just over 1 MMT.

Export Sales data will be released shortly, with traders surveyed by Reuters looking for between 0.5-1.2 MMT in 2026/27 soybean sales in the week of 10/8. Sales for 2027/28 are seen in a range of 0-50,000 MT. Soybean sales are seen in a range of 200,000 to 60,000 MT, with bean oil expected to be between sales of 0-10,000 MT.

NOPA data was released on Thursday, with a total of just 196.3 mbu of soybeans crushed in September, down 0.8% from last year and 4.46% below the August total. That was well below estimates coming in. Soybean oil stocks were down 12.35% from the end of August and 15.31% below last year at 1.053 billion lbs. That was the lowest stocks total since November 2014.

CONAB estimates the 2026/27 Brazilian soybean crop at 181.6 MMT, up just 0.7% from a year ago and well below the 186 MMT estimate from USDA. Acreage was just 1.43% higher at 49.3 million hectares (121.84 million acres), and the smallest yr/yr increase since 2011/12.
